result.question: Discuss the quantitative instruments of monetary policy available to the Reserve Bank of India. How has the monetary policy framework changed since 2016? (Answer in 250 words)

directives.meaning: Look at the issue from more than one side, with reasons, and reach a balanced view.

sentences.text: Monetary policy is the RBI's management of money supply and interest rates to maintain price stability with growth.
Its quantitative instruments regulate the overall volume and cost of credit.
The Cash Reserve Ratio is the share of a bank's deposits kept with the RBI in cash; raising it shrinks lendable funds.
The Statutory Liquidity Ratio requires banks to hold part of their deposits with themselves in liquid assets such as cash, gold and approved securities.
Open market operations are the RBI's purchases and sales of government securities in the market.
When the RBI buys government securities in the open market, it withdraws liquidity from the banking system and reduces the money supply.
The repo rate is the rate at which the RBI lends short-term funds to banks against government securities, and it serves as the policy rate.
The reverse repo rate is the rate at which banks borrow overnight from the RBI when they face a liquidity shortage.
Since 2022, the Standing Deposit Facility, which absorbs surplus liquidity without requiring collateral, has replaced the fixed-rate reverse repo as the corridor's floor.
The Marginal Standing Facility lets banks borrow overnight from the RBI at a penal rate above the repo rate, and the Bank Rate is now aligned with it.
The framework changed when the RBI Act, 1934 was amended in 2016 to give statutory backing to flexible inflation targeting.
The Government, in consultation with the RBI, sets the inflation target in terms of consumer price inflation.
A six-member Monetary Policy Committee, chaired by the RBI Governor who has a casting vote, now decides the policy repo rate.
Faster transmission to lending rates, aided by external benchmark-linked loans, will decide these tools' effectiveness.
